# Cindrasec

> Attack-surface and AI/LLM security studio based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Automated
> external exposure monitoring and adversarial testing of LLM-backed systems for
> founders, SMEs and AI vendors. Verification-first and authorized-only: testing
> begins after a signed Rules of Engagement, findings are validated before they
> are reported, and what was not tested is stated explicitly.

Founded 2025-07 by Md. Azmol Haque Rony. Services are fixed-scope and fixed-price;
no hourly billing. Work is delivered in English and Bengali.

## Services

- [Attack Surface Snapshot](https://cindrasec.com/#pricing): One-time external
  assessment of a domain and its subdomains — certificate-transparency enumeration,
  live-host discovery, credentials exposed in public JavaScript bundles, security
  posture, subdomain-takeover risk. Passive-first: discovery uses public records
  rather than traffic against the target. 3–5 days, $250–600 (৳15,000–25,000).
- [Watch](https://cindrasec.com/#pricing): Continuous monitoring after a Snapshot,
  with monthly diff reports and alerts when new exposure appears. $150–500/month
  (৳5,000–12,000).
- [AI/LLM Security Assessment](https://cindrasec.com/#services): Adversarial testing
  of chatbots, agents, MCP servers and LLM features — direct and indirect prompt
  injection, system-prompt and data exposure, agent and tool abuse, MCP tool-surface
  review covering tool poisoning and consent flows. Results are reported as rates
  across repeated trials with confidence intervals, not single pass/fail anecdotes.
  2–5 days, $2,000–8,000 (৳40,000–1,50,000).
- [Productized Gig](https://cindrasec.com/#pricing): One tightly-scoped check with a
  single deliverable and a price agreed up front. 2–4 hours, $150–500 (৳7,000–15,000).

## Published research

- [Prompt-injection resistance is content-dependent](https://cindrasec.com/research/2026-07-prompt-injection-content-dependent/):
  Measured study using NVIDIA's garak scanner against Llama 3.2 (3B) self-hosted on a
  Raspberry Pi 5. Two probes from the promptinject family, 256 trials each. The same
  injection technique succeeded 46.9% of the time (95% CI 41.0–53.1%) when the target
  string was mildly toxic, but only 10.2% of the time (95% CI 6.6–14.1%) when it was
  overtly violent — a 4.6x difference in attack success from the same technique,
  changing only the goal. The confidence intervals do not overlap. Conclusion: a
  model's prompt-injection resistance is a distribution, not a single score, so one
  benchmark number can be off by multiples from the threat that actually matters to
  a given deployment. Safety training concentrates its strongest refusals on overtly
  harmful categories, which leaves milder categories comparatively exposed — the
  attack that reads as worse to a human is the one the model resists best.
- [Exposed IAM configuration in a frontend bundle (Google VRP)](https://cindrasec.com/research/2026-05-exposed-iam-frontend-google-vrp/):
  Disclosure writeup covering an identity-and-access-management configuration left
  reachable in a client-side bundle, reported through Google's Vulnerability Reward
  Program. Full reproduction and translations into 9 languages are on GitHub:
  https://github.com/azmolhaque/security-writeups

## Open-source tools

- [SecretNode](https://github.com/azmolhaque/secretnode): Passive credential-leak and
  attack-surface scanner. Enumerates subdomains via certificate transparency, probes
  live hosts, and scans JavaScript bundles and historical archive copies for exposed
  secrets. Ships a CLI, a GitHub Action, and SARIF output for pipeline gating.
  Default-passive; live verification of a finding against a provider API is opt-in
  behind an explicit flag and stops at establishing whether a credential is valid.

## Policies

- [Rules of Engagement](https://cindrasec.com/legal/Cindrasec_RoE_Authorization.docx):
  Authorization document signed before any testing begins.
- [security.txt](https://cindrasec.com/.well-known/security.txt): RFC 9116 disclosure
  contact.
- Data handling: assessment data is self-hosted, encrypted at rest, deleted on
  request, and auto-purged 30 days after delivery. The site sets no tracking cookies
  and loads no third-party scripts beyond the contact-form endpoint.
